title: The Toric Code
summary: A stabilizer code on a torus: errors are strings, syndromes are their endpoints, logical operators are loops.
objectives: Compute which plaquettes detect an X error chain on the torus.
Tell a contractible error loop (a product of stabilizers) from a non-contractible one (a logical operator).
Find the code distance of a small torus by searching for the shortest undetected logical chain.
Explain why a single error creates a pair of syndrome defects.
mission: Edges of an L×L torus are tuples ("h", r, c) and ("v", r, c), and a chain is a set of edges carrying X errors. plaquette_edges(L, r, c) is given. Write defects(L, chain), which returns the list of plaquettes (r, c) whose Z-stabilizer anticommutes with the chain. Write logical_class(L, chain), which for a chain with no defects returns (a, b): the parities of the number of its edges in the row ("h", 0, c) and in the column ("v", r, 0). Then search all chains on the 3×3 torus by increasing size and store in distance the size of the smallest chain that has no defects and logical_class other than (0, 0).

prediction.question: A single X error acts on one edge of the torus. How many plaquette stabilizers anticommute with it?
options: Two, the plaquettes on either side of the edge
Four, the plaquettes at the corners of the edge
prediction.explanation: Every edge borders exactly two plaquettes, so X on that edge flips the eigenvalue of both. Defects always come in pairs for a chain with open ends, and extending the chain by one edge moves one of the two defects.

hints: A plaquette (r, c) fires when the chain contains an odd number of its four edges. Loop over all L² plaquettes, count with plaquette_edges(L, r, c), and keep those with odd count. A chain is a set, so "edge in chain" is a membership test.

logical_class counts edges of two fixed Z-loops: the row of horizontal edges ("h", 0, c) and the column of vertical edges ("v", r, 0). Each count is taken modulo 2. A product of stars gives (0, 0); a loop that wraps around the torus gives a non-zero class.

Use itertools.combinations(edges, w) for w = 1, 2, 3, … with edges = [(t, r, c) for t in "hv" for r in range(L) for c in range(L)]. For each chain (as a set), test that defects is empty and logical_class is not (0, 0). Stop at the first w that has one.
